links.outcome: Reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without FSLS; overreliance assessed via change analysis
links.effect: Groups containing 66% of readers improved accuracy by 12%-15% with FSLS (p<.05); other groups had no net change (p>.75); no reader adopted FSLS errors uncritically.
links.quote: Machine learning‐assisted identification with the FSLS improved the performance of groups containing 66% of readers by 12%–15%, but other readers could not effectively identify when to change their diagnosis based on the FSLS.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with the AI score in the intended workflow versus history alone
links.effect: Reference group accuracy rose from 41% to 60% (+19%) and near-highest group from 67% to 82% (+15%) with FSLS; other groups no net change.
links.quote: The group of average readers (Group 5) was able to understand the FSLS enough to improve their accuracy from 44% to 60%.

links.outcome: Whether users detect incorrect AI outputs; rates of being persuaded or misled by FSLS
links.effect: Group 2 was never misled; Group 5 improved 21% from persuasion and lost 4% from being misled; readers persuaded in only 30%-45% of cases when FSLS was correct.
links.quote: The accuracy of the near highest performance group (Group 2) improved because they were persuaded by the FSLS, but they were never misled (Figures 4 and S4–S6).

links.outcome: Worsening performance from FSLS use of sex and trauma features perpetuating disparities
links.effect: No worsening performance was observed when the FSLS was provided, so concerns about perpetuating sex-driven disparities were not seen in the data.
links.quote: However, we did not observe worsening performance when the FSLS was provided, which indicated that these initial concerns were not seen in the data.

links.outcome: Potential deskilling or threshold shift among readers using FSLS
links.effect: Intermediate Group 4 net accuracy fell 4% (p=.92), with a 19% increase in FDS predictive value and a 10% decrease in epilepsy predictive value; AUC rose 1%; no clear deskilling.
links.quote: Although the net accuracy of readers in intermediate Group 4 reduced numerically by 4% (post‐FSLS difference, p = .92), that difference may have corresponded to a shift in the threshold of concern for FDS
